# Talk to ChatGPT by voice on your phone while cooking or driving

> **In short:** With the ChatGPT phone app you can have a spoken conversation with the assistant — ask out loud, hear the answer, follow up — hands-free. Setup takes about a minute; the free plan includes limited Voice time, and paid plans give you more.

By the end of this guide you'll have ChatGPT's voice mode working on your phone, ready to chat with you out loud while your hands are busy. This is for anyone who wants a hands-free way to brainstorm, settle a small argument, plan dinner, or just keep a conversation going without staring at a screen.

## Before you start
- **An iPhone or Android phone** with the free ChatGPT app installed (App Store on iPhone, Google Play on Android). Tablet works too.
- **A ChatGPT account** — the free plan is enough to try voice mode, and sign-up takes about two minutes with any email address.
- **About five minutes** total: two for install and sign-in, three for your first conversation.
- **A calm-ish first moment.** Test voice mode somewhere quiet first (a kitchen counter, a parked car, a quiet room). Once you know it works, you can take it anywhere.

## Step 1 — Install the ChatGPT app
Open your phone's app store — the **App Store** on iPhone, **Google Play** on Android — and search for "ChatGPT". The official app is published by OpenAI and shows a black square icon with a white, interlocking flower-like logo. Tap **Install** or **Get**, then wait for the download to finish.

If the store search is crowded with lookalikes, ignore anything that asks for payment upfront or has a different publisher name. The official one is free and clearly labeled "OpenAI" as the developer.

You'll know it worked when the ChatGPT app icon is on your home screen and tapping it opens the app's sign-in or chat screen.

💬 Example: search term to copy — `ChatGPT`

## Step 2 — Sign in or create a free account
When the app opens, you'll see a **Sign up** button and a **Log in** link at the bottom. If you already have a ChatGPT account, tap Log in and enter your email and password. If not, tap Sign up — you'll need an email address you can check (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, or any other works) plus your name and birthday.

Sign-up usually sends a verification code to your email. After that, you land directly on the free plan. Voice works for every logged-in user; on the free plan your Voice time is limited, and paid plans such as ChatGPT Plus give you more of it.

You'll know it worked when you see a new, empty chat with a message box at the bottom.

💬 Example: sign-up email — any address you check regularly; the verification code arrives in your inbox within a minute.

## Step 3 — Tap the Voice icon to start a spoken conversation
In the message bar at the bottom of the chat screen, tap the **Voice** icon. Don't mix it up with the microphone: in ChatGPT the microphone is **Dictation**, which turns one recording into editable text that you then send yourself — nothing is read back to you. Voice is the live, spoken back-and-forth this guide is about.

The first time, the app asks for permission to use your microphone — allow it — and then asks you to choose a preferred voice. Pick any one; you can change it later in Step 6.

You'll know it worked when the Voice screen opens and ChatGPT is ready to hear you.

💬 Example: tap the Voice icon once and start talking — you don't need to press and hold anything.

## Step 4 — Ask your first spoken question
Once Voice opens, talk in a normal voice, as if a friend were sitting across from you. Speak **one clear sentence at a time**, then pause for a moment. When you stop talking, ChatGPT responds out loud through your phone's speaker, and the conversation is saved as a text transcript in the chat.

If you're in a noisy kitchen, hold the phone a little closer to your mouth or step away from the blender. If you're in the car, use Bluetooth or a phone mount so you don't need to pick the device up. Keep your eyes where they need to be — on the road, on the cutting board — and let your ears do the work.

You'll know it worked when you hear ChatGPT's spoken answer come back through the speaker within a couple of seconds, in a voice that sounds like a real person rather than a robot.

💬 Example: *"I'm making dinner with chicken, rice, and broccoli. What sauce can I whip up in ten minutes with stuff I probably already have?"*

## Step 5 — Keep the conversation going naturally
Voice mode works like a real chat — you can interrupt, ask follow-ups, or change direction mid-answer. If ChatGPT starts rambling, just say **"shorter please"** or **"give me the top three."** If you want to switch topics entirely, just ask the new question; you don't need to say "new topic" first.

Need a moment of quiet? Tap the **microphone** control on the Voice screen to mute yourself, and tap it again to unmute. You can also keep talking while you use another app or after your phone locks — the background setting lives under **Settings → Voice**. Your spoken conversation is saved as text in your chat history, so you can scroll back later or copy a recipe into your notes.

You'll know it worked when you can fire off three or four follow-up questions in a row without tapping anything.

💬 Example: follow-ups — *"Make it spicy."* → *"Do I have everything for that?"* → *"Okay, last step by step while I cook."*

## Step 6 — Change the voice or stop the session
To swap the voice, open **Settings → Voice**, then select **Voice** and pick from the list — each one has its own character, such as Breeze (animated and earnest) or Spruce (calm and affirming). If you change it in the middle of a Voice conversation, a new voice call starts in the same chat. On the same screen, **Language** helps if Voice keeps mishearing you, and **Start with Voice** makes a new, empty chat open straight into Voice — handy when your hands are full.

To finish, tap the exit control on the Voice screen. Your conversation stays in your chat history with the spoken words saved as text. Next time you want hands-free, tap the Voice icon again — it keeps your chosen voice.

You'll know it worked when the next voice session greets you in the voice you picked last time.

💬 Example: the voices shown vary by region and account — try two or three for a few seconds each and trust the one that feels easiest to listen to for a long chat.

## Common mistakes
- **Tapping the microphone instead of Voice.** The microphone starts Dictation: it turns one recording into text that you send, and nothing is read aloud. If you want ChatGPT to talk back, use the Voice icon.
- **Trusting the transcript word for word.** OpenAI notes that Voice transcripts are not verbatim records and may not exactly match what was said. For anything that must be exact — a phone number, an address, a measurement — check it in the text afterward.
- **Setting things up while driving.** Open the app, pick your voice and start Voice before you pull out; OpenAI's own advice is to avoid interacting with your device while the vehicle is moving. On a supported iPhone, ChatGPT also works in Apple CarPlay. For anything visual — long answers, lists, links — pull over first, or hand the phone to a passenger.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You're chopping vegetables with wet hands and need to convert cups to grams — just ask out loud. You're folding laundry and want a podcast-style recap of the news — voice mode can walk you through it while your hands stay busy.
- **For your business or work:** On a long drive between meetings, you can brainstorm ideas, talk through a presentation outline, or rehearse what you'll say to a client. Save anything sensitive for text mode, where you can review and edit before sending.
- **If you're just getting started:** Try the simplest possible thing first — ask it the time in another city, or to tell you a knock-knock joke. That removes the pressure and shows you how natural the back-and-forth feels before you bring it into the kitchen or the car.

## Try it now
Open the ChatGPT app, tap the Voice icon once, and ask: *"I'm about to cook with [whatever's in your fridge right now]. What can I make in twenty minutes?"* Then just listen, follow up, and let your hands stay where they're needed.
